h: Island Hopping Between Animals and Adventures
p: Owl & Monkey Haven is a smaller, quieter visit, which makes it easy to fit into a busy island holiday. Plan an hour or two, catch a talk if one's running, and take your time at each enclosure. Some of the owls are masters of camouflage, so give the kids a challenge to spot them before you read the signs. Because it's a sanctuary, every visit helps with the cost of caring for animals that can't go back to the wild, which makes the trip feel worthwhile.

Getting to the island is part of the adventure. Car ferries run from Portsmouth, Southampton and Lymington, and there are faster foot-passenger services too. Once you're there, it's compact enough to pack plenty into a few days.

Families have loads of choice. Blackgang Chine, on the south coast, is a long-running clifftop theme park with dinosaurs, pirates and fairy-tale lands. Dinosaur Isle in Sandown celebrates the island's rich haul of dinosaur fossils, many found along its crumbling cliffs, and the nearby Isle of Wight Zoo is another big animal day out. History lovers can visit Osborne, Queen Victoria's seaside home, or climb the walls of Carisbrooke Castle, where you can watch donkeys work the old wheel at the well. The Isle of Wight Steam Railway at Havenstreet runs heritage trains through gentle countryside. And keep your eyes open as you travel round: the island is one of the few places in southern England where you can still spot wild red squirrels.
